Alright, let me think this through. I'm getting on in years and it's just me in the house now, so labor is tight. My 20 mu is split roughly — about 14 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 6 mu in cotton over on the field my father used to work. I've been doing this 35 years, so I mostly do what's worked for me, with small changes.

**Wheat (already in the ground from last October, 14 mu):**
The wheat went in around early October like always. Now spring's here and I need to think about topdressing and water. Last year I got around 450 kg/mu — not bad. I put down about 2 bags of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, and I'll topdress urea at jointing, maybe 10 kg/mu. If the spring's dry I'll water three times — before jointing, at heading, and filling. Water costs money from the well so I don't do four unless it's a bad drought year. My neighbor老王 has been cutting back on irrigation and his yield dropped, so I'm not changing.

**Maize (goes in right after wheat harvest in mid-June, same 14 mu):**
Tight turnaround — maybe 5 days between wheat combining and getting maize in. I hire the custom planter because I can't do it alone at my age. Buy the regular hybrid seed, nothing fancy. Put down one shot of compound fertilizer at planting, about 30 kg/mu. If it rains well I don't irrigate at all; usually I end up watering once at tasseling if July is dry. I expect around 500 kg/mu if the season's normal.

**Cotton (6 mu, plant late April):**
Cotton's hard work — I'm thinking of reducing it next year because picking is killing my back and I have to hire help. This year I'll still do it. Seed from the village supplier, plastic mulch like everyone uses here. About 2 bags compound at planting plus some urea later when it's growing. Spray for bollworm a few times — the pink bollworm has been bad. Irrigate twice. Picking I'll have to hire 2-3 days of labor each time, three pickings.

I'm keeping a bit of cash reserve because I'm alone and any medical emergency has to come from my pocket.
